The short version

Mass Reaction is an endless balance puzzle for iPhone. This policy explains, in plain terms, what the game and this website process, what they do not, where the data goes and how long anything is kept.

  • No accounts, no sign-up, no names. You can play without giving us your name or email address.
  • Your progress stays with you. Your best score, settings and seen tips stay on your iPhone; your stash of special balls is kept in your own iCloud account. We cannot see either.
  • Apple handles payments and the leaderboard. Purchases go through the App Store, and scores go to Game Center if you are signed in. We never receive your card details.
  • Game statistics and crash reports, outside Europe only. If your App Store country is outside the European Economic Area, the United Kingdom and Switzerland, the game sends gameplay events and crash reports to Google’s Firebase. They describe games, menus and purchases, not your moves, and contain no name or email address. In the EEA, the UK and Switzerland the game sends neither. Elsewhere they are always on; deleting the game stops them.
  • Tracking only if you allow it. Outside those countries, iOS asks once, at the start of your second game, whether the game may use your advertising identifier. If you allow it, Google uses it to estimate the age range and interests of our players. If you decline, nothing in the game changes.
  • No advertising in the game, no sale of data, and no cookies inside the game.
  • The website uses analytics cookies only with your consent, given in its cookie banner.

Who is responsible

Mass Reaction and massreaction.app are developed and published by Yulia Shishkina, an independent software developer in Luxembourg, who is the data controller for the personal data described in this policy (“we”, “us”). The game is designed to avoid collecting directly identifying personal data wherever possible. For any privacy question or request, .

On your iPhone

The game keeps a few things on your iPhone: your best score; your settings (sound and vibration); which special-ball tips you have already seen; a copy of your stash; and a few counters for the game statistics described below (how many games you have started, your best level, whether you have made a purchase, the first version you installed, and a short summary of a game left unfinished when the app was closed, which is sent at the next launch). This information stays on the device, is not sent to us except as part of those statistics, and is removed when you delete the game. The only permission the game may ask for is the tracking permission described below; it does not ask for access to your camera, photos, microphone, contacts or location.

Your stash in iCloud

If iCloud is turned on for the game, it keeps counters of the special balls you have bought and used in your private iCloud key-value storage, so your stash follows you to your other devices and survives reinstalling. To keep devices from overwriting each other, the game creates a random identifier for each device; it is not linked to your name, Apple ID or any advertising identifier.

This data is stored by Apple in your iCloud account under Apple’s Privacy Policy. We cannot see or access it. If iCloud is off, the stash is kept only on that device and is lost if the game is deleted.

In-app purchases

Special-ball packs are optional and sold through Apple’s in-app purchase system. Apple handles the payment; we never receive your card details or billing address. The game receives a confirmation of the transaction from Apple so it can add the items to your stash.

Game Center

If you are signed in to Game Center, the game submits your score at the end of a run to the Mass Reaction leaderboard. Depending on your Game Center settings, your nickname and score can be visible to other players. Game Center is operated by Apple; you can manage your profile and visibility in your iPhone settings.

Game statistics and crash reports

Where they run. The game uses two Google services: Firebase Analytics for game statistics and Firebase Crashlytics for crash reports. Both are off when the game starts. They turn on only once the game knows the country or region of your App Store account and it is outside the European Economic Area, the United Kingdom and Switzerland. In those countries, and as long as the country is unknown, the game sends no statistics and no crash reports and never shows the tracking prompt; events from the first moments after launch wait on your iPhone and are then deleted unsent. If you switch your App Store account to another country, the game checks again.

What the game sends. Events about games and menus, not about your moves: a game started or ended, with how it ended, the level, score and duration, the number of balls dropped and the special balls used; a special ball released from your stash; the power-up offer shown, chosen or closed; the shop opened, and a purchase started, completed, cancelled, failed or refunded, with the product, price and currency; the panels you open and the buttons you press in them; the special-ball tips shown; and your answer to the tracking prompt. It also sets a few summary values: how many games you have played (in ranges), your best level, whether you have made a purchase, the first version you installed and your tracking answer. Drops, tilts, throws and taps on the board are not sent.

What Firebase adds. To deliver and count these events, Firebase Analytics processes technical data: the app version and whether it is an App Store or test build, the iOS version, the device model and language, session times, an approximate location (country, region and city) derived from your IP address, which Google Analytics does not store, and pseudonymous identifiers: the Firebase app-instance identifier and Apple’s identifier for vendor (IDFV). It also records standard events such as the first launch, sessions, app updates and iOS updates. These identifiers are not a name or an account ID. We do not combine them with contact details, iCloud data or Game Center profiles.

Crash reports. If the game crashes, Crashlytics sends a report at the next launch: where in the code the crash happened, the app and iOS versions, the device model and its state at that moment, the time, a random Crashlytics installation identifier, the last panel shown, the game number and level, and the most recent game-statistics events listed above. We use crash reports only to find and fix bugs.

Your choice. The game has no switch for game statistics and crash reports: where they run, they are always on. Deleting the game stops both, removes its counters and resets the Firebase identifiers, so a later installation is not linked to the earlier data. You can also object to them by writing to us (see Your rights); as the data carries no name or email address, we may not be able to find the data that came from your iPhone, and if so we will tell you. See how Google uses information from sites and apps that use its services.

Permission to track

Where game statistics run, iOS asks you once, when your second game starts, whether Mass Reaction may track your activity across other companies’ apps and websites. The prompt is never shown in the EEA, the UK or Switzerland.

If you tap “Allow”, Firebase Analytics also receives your iPhone’s advertising identifier (IDFA). Google can link it with information it holds from other apps and websites to estimate the age range, gender and interests of our players. We see these estimates only as aggregated reports in Google Analytics, never for an individual player. Apple calls this tracking. The game shows no ads and does not use the identifier for advertising, and it tells Google, through Google’s consent settings, that the data may not be used for personalised advertising or sent to Google for advertising purposes.

If you tap “Ask App Not to Track”, the game cannot read the advertising identifier and works exactly the same. You can change your answer at any time in your iPhone’s Settings → Privacy & Security → Tracking.

This website

massreaction.app has no advertising trackers, accounts or forms. Fonts and images are served with the site rather than loaded from other services. Two small scripts run on the pages: one builds our support address when you click a contact button and stores nothing; the other shows the cookie banner and remembers your answer in your browser’s local storage (not a cookie), so we do not ask again on every page.

To deliver and protect the pages, our hosting provider in Germany and Cloudflare, which sits in front of the site, process technical connection data such as your IP address, browser type, the page requested and the time. This data is used only to run and secure the site and is not combined with other information.

Website analytics

If you click “Accept” in the cookie banner, the site loads Google Analytics 4, a service of Google Ireland Limited, Gordon House, Barrow Street, Dublin 4, Ireland. If you click “Decline” or ignore the banner, it is not loaded and nothing is sent to Google.

With your consent, Google Analytics sets two first-party cookies, _ga and _ga_BN36B66LGS, which tell visits apart and last up to two years. It records the pages you view, scrolling, clicks on links to other sites and similar interactions, along with your browser and device type, screen size, the page you came from, and an approximate location derived from your IP address. Google Analytics 4 does not log or store IP addresses. Google signals and ad personalisation are turned off.

You can withdraw your consent at any time: click “Cookie settings” at the bottom of any page and choose “Decline”. The site then deletes the Analytics cookies and stops loading Google Analytics. .

When you contact us

If you email us, we receive your email address, your message and anything you choose to include. We use it only to answer you. When you write from the game (Settings → About → Contact Support), the letter opens in your own email app and already includes the game’s version, your iPhone model, the iOS version and your App Store country, to help us answer; you can see and delete them before sending, and nothing is sent unless you send the letter. Mail to our support address is forwarded by Cloudflare Email Routing to a mailbox hosted by Google. Please do not send card details, passwords or other sensitive information.

What we do not collect

  • names, phone numbers or email addresses in the game;
  • account credentials (there are no accounts);
  • your precise location, photos, camera, microphone or contacts;
  • your moves on the board;
  • payment card data (Apple handles payments);
  • the advertising identifier (IDFA), unless you allow tracking;
  • any game statistics or crash reports if your App Store country is in the EEA, the UK or Switzerland;
  • health or financial data.

We do not sell personal data, and the game shows no ads.

International transfers

Google, Cloudflare and Apple may process data outside the European Economic Area, including in the United States. For such transfers we rely on appropriate safeguards under the GDPR: the EU–US Data Privacy Framework where the provider is certified, and the European Commission’s Standard Contractual Clauses where applicable.

Legal bases

  • Performance of a contract (Art. 6(1)(b) GDPR): delivering the special balls you buy and keeping your stash.
  • Our legitimate interests (Art. 6(1)(f) GDPR): keeping the website secure and available, answering your messages, and measuring game statistics and crash reports to fix problems and balance the game. You can object to game statistics and crash reports at any time (see Your rights); deleting the game stops both.
  • Your consent (Art. 6(1)(a) GDPR): website analytics cookies, which you can withdraw under “Cookie settings”, and the advertising identifier in the game, given in the iOS tracking prompt and withdrawn in your iPhone’s Settings → Privacy & Security → Tracking.
  • Your choices: turning on iCloud or signing in to Game Center.

Game statistics, crash reports and connection data are pseudonymous rather than anonymous, so the GDPR may apply to them; we do not claim otherwise.

How long we keep data

  • Data on your iPhone: until you delete the game. The summary of an unfinished game is sent at the next launch, or deleted if that launch comes more than 30 days later or statistics are off.
  • Your stash in iCloud: in your iCloud account, under your control.
  • Game statistics: according to the data-retention setting of the Google Analytics property behind Firebase. Google Analytics keeps event-level data for at most 14 months; after that only aggregated reports remain.
  • Crash reports: 90 days in Firebase Crashlytics.
  • Website analytics: event-level data for two months and user-level data for 14 months; after that only aggregated reports remain.
  • Connection data at the host and Cloudflare: according to their log-retention policies.
  • Support emails: only as long as needed to handle your request and any follow-up.

Your rights

Where the GDPR applies, you may have the right to access, correct or erase your personal data, to receive a copy of it, to object to or restrict its processing, and to withdraw consent. To make a request, . Because the game has no accounts, we often cannot find statistics that belong to a particular player; we will not collect extra identifying data just to do so unless you ask us to. Data held by Apple, including iCloud, purchases and Game Center, is managed through your Apple account.

You can also complain to a supervisory authority. In Luxembourg, this is the Commission nationale pour la protection des données (CNPD).

Children

Mass Reaction is a general-audience puzzle game. It does not ask anyone, including children, for personal information, and it does not knowingly collect personal data from children. Purchases and Game Center are subject to the parental controls of the Apple account used on the device.

Security

  • collecting as little as possible, leaving your moves out of game statistics and avoiding accounts;
  • keeping game progress on your device and in your own iCloud;
  • encrypting the website and all game traffic in transit (HTTPS);
  • restricting access to the server and to the analytics properties.

No online service can guarantee absolute security, but the game is designed to hold as little identifiable data as possible.

Changes to this policy

We update this policy when the game, the website, our providers or our data practices change, before the change reaches you. The date at the top always reflects the current version, which is published at https://massreaction.app/privacy.html.
